subject: LLM response exportability & no-weights training commitment — evidence and escrow options
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@meditechlabs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: exportability & training opt-out evidence for ND-3491

Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal and engineering at Meditech Labs are aligned on the product fit, but we have a couple of compliance blockers before procurement can sign ND-3491. The two items they asked me to confirm: 1) a clear, auditable guarantee that our customer content and LLM responses will not be used to further train or tune Redwood models (no-weights/no-train commitment), and 2) a repeatable exportability path for response artifacts and metadata (for our auditors).

Specifically they want:
- A plain-language attestation we can include with the contract stating that Redwood will not use customer inputs or generated responses for model training except as expressly permitted in the DPA.
- The exact set of artifacts we could export on request (responses, prompt history, token-level metadata, retention timestamps) and the formats (CSV/NDJSON preferred).
- Examples of technical evidence you can provide (logs, configuration snapshots, signed attestations, hash checks) to show the environment is isolated from model training pipelines.

We can provide the DPA redlines (attached) and a short spec from our security team about the export schema (I attached exportability_spec.xlsx). Can you confirm whether Redwood offers any escrow or escrow-like options for response archives? If not, what is the typical operational path customers take to get a certified export for audits?

No need for long answers — high level + any attachments/examples will do. We have an internal review Friday, so if we could get something by Thursday EOD that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Head of Privacy & Security
Meditech Labs

Attachments: exportability_spec.xlsx
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@meditechlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: exportability & training opt-out evidence for ND-3491

Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask and the spec — that helps a lot. Short answers up front, then a proposed evidence pack and options: 

1) No-weights / no-train commitment: yes, Redwood is prepared to include a contractual no-training commitment for Meditech Labs where we explicitly exclude customer inputs and generated responses from any training or model improvement processes. We have an existing DPA clause that covers this; Marissa, Priyom and I can provide a redlined version for ND-3491.

2) Exportable artifacts: Redwood can produce a one-time certified export bundle containing: prompt/response pairs (NDJSON), per-request metadata (request id, timestamp, model variant, route), token counts, and an integrity manifest (SHA256 hashes). We cannot export internal model weights or gradients (those are never customer-specific). The export can be encrypted and delivered via a signed S3 link or pushed to a customer-managed bucket in the same cloud region.

Evidence & operational options (pick one):
- Attestation + logs (standard): We provide a signed attestation from Engineering and a log extract showing requests processed in an isolated serving fleet (includes request ids and timestamps).
- Escrow-style archive (recommended for audits): We can create immutable response archives (GZIP+NDJSON) stored with WORM settings in a customer-designated storage location for a contractually agreed retention period. Redwood can facilitate read-only access for auditors.
- Live isolation demo + config snapshot: For higher assurance, Priyom can run a short demo showing that serving instances used for your traffic are not connected to any training pipelines and provide configuration snapshots and network ACLs.

I attached an initial draft attestation and the DPA redlines we typically propose. We can tighten language if your legal team has specific wording preferences. Would you prefer the escrow archive route or attestation+logs? If escrow, we can propose a partner (we've used IronSight Escrow previously) and estimate cost/time.

Happy to hop on 30 minutes tomorrow — Priyom can do a technical walkthrough if helpful.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Product — Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_redlines_v3.pdf, jw_attestation_draft.txt
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@meditechlabs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novamark Legal <contracts@novamark.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: exportability & training opt-out evidence for ND-3491

Thanks Jonas — that roadmap looks good. Legal is leaning toward the escrow-style archive plus a signed attestation. Two clarifications from security: 
- Can Redwood produce the integrity manifest at the time of export and provide the manifest signed by a Redwood key? We want a cryptographic chain-of-custody for each archive.
- For the audit window, we need read-only auditor access with IP allowlisting for auditor CIDRs (no broad public links).

If you can confirm those two points and share high-level costs/timeline for standing up an escrow archive, I can route to procurement. Our target is to close before the end of December.

Elena

Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: exportability & training opt-out evidence for ND-3491

Elena / Elena's procurement team —

Forwarding a short plan so Legal has everything in one place. Per your preference we will proceed with the escrow-style archive + signed attestation. Key points: 

- Chain-of-custody & signed manifest: Redwood will generate a SHA256 manifest at export time and sign the manifest with our code-signing key. We will include the public key fingerprint in the attestation.
- Auditor access: Exports will be staged to a customer-designated S3 bucket with forced TLS, object-level encryption, and bucket policies that restrict access to specific auditor IP CIDRs you provide. We will not provide public links.
- Operational timeline & cost: Initial setup (partner onboarding, bucket ACLs, WORM config) — 7 business days after contract execution. One-time setup fee: $6,500. Per-archive processing and certification: $850. Estimated time to produce the first archive after request: 48 business hours.
- Contract language: Attached is DPA_redlines_v3.pdf with the no-train clause highlighted. We will add a short escrow addendum that captures retention, access procedures, and attestations.

Next steps: Please confirm the auditor CIDR ranges and whether you want Redwood to propose an escrow partner (we can do that) or if you will provide a partner. If procurement agrees to the one-time setup fee we will queue this as critical and target a Dec calendar close.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_redlines_v3.pdf
